T: Meet the family. Drop the strata.
D: A tightly wound woman meets her boyfriend's free-spirited family over a very awkward Christmas.
P: Serve breakfast when Meredith's strata hits the floor.
S: Bacon wrapped sausages glazed in maple, cranberry mustard dip

Chipolatas wrapped in streaky bacon and roasted until crisp and sticky, with a cranberry mustard dip for the family to fight over. Wrap 20 chipolatas in half rashers of streaky bacon from 10 rashers. Lay on a lined tray and roast at 200C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Brush with 2 tbsp maple syrup for the last 5 minutes. Mix 150g cranberry sauce with 2 tbsp wholegrain mustard for dipping and serve hot on toothpicks.
Crusty loaf sliced deep and stuffed with garlic herb butter

A soft bread loaf scored and stuffed with garlic, parsley and parmesan butter, baked until crusty and passed around to tear apart. Cut a 500g crusty loaf in deep diagonal slices every 2cm, without cutting through the base. Mash 100g soft butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 3 tbsp chopped parsley and 30g grated parmesan. Push the butter into every cut. Wrap in foil and bake at 190C for 15 minutes, then open the foil and bake 8 minutes more until crisp and golden.
M: Baked bread and egg casserole with ham, spinach and gruyère

A baked layered bread and egg pudding with ham, gruyère, spinach and Dijon, puffed and golden on top, ideally kept off the floor. Butter a 2L baking dish. Layer 6 thick slices of day-old bread, torn, with 200g diced ham, 100g wilted baby spinach and 150g grated gruyère. Whisk 6 eggs with 500ml milk, 1 tbsp Dijon, salt and pepper and pour over. Press down, cover and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight. Bake at 180C for 45 minutes until puffed and golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with tomato relish.
Sybil's lemon and thyme roast chicken
Christmas Eve, every Stone at the table and nobody holding back
Whole chicken roasted over lemon and thyme with garlic butter under the skin, potatoes in the pan juices.
W: Soft rolled scrolls with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon

Soft brioche-style scrolls rolled with brown sugar, cinnamon and butter, baked golden and smothered in tangy cream cheese icing. Roll 500g pizza dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with 60g soft butter, then sprinkle with 80g brown sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Roll up from the long side and cut into 12 scrolls. Pack into a greased 24cm tin, cover and rest 30 minutes. Bake at 190C for 22 minutes. Beat 120g cream cheese, 30g butter, 150g icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla and spread over the warm scrolls.
K: Strong coffee topped with frothy eggnog milk and nutmeg

Strong coffee topped with steamed spiced eggnog milk and grated nutmeg, with a splash of brandy for the grown-ups. Kids get the eggnog milk on its own. Heat 500ml milk with 150ml thickened cream, 3 tbsp caster sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Whisk 2 egg yolks in a bowl, pour in the hot milk while whisking, then return to the pan and stir over low heat for 3 minutes until slightly thick. Brew 400ml strong coffee and divide between 4 mugs. Froth the eggnog milk, pour over and grate nutmeg on top. Add 20ml brandy per mug if wanted.

dishes.n: Sybil's lemon and thyme roast chicken
dishes.make_ahead: Make the garlic butter up to 3 days ahead; butter the chicken up to 1 day ahead and keep it in the fridge

steps.text: Mix the butter with the garlic, thyme leaves, zest of a lemon and salt.
Push the butter under the chicken skin and put the halved lemons and thyme stalks in the cavity.
Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top.
Roast at 200C until the juices run clear.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carve and spoon the pan juices over.

veg.n: Sybil's lemon and thyme roast cauliflower
veg.make_ahead: Make the garlic butter up to 3 days ahead; roast on the night

steps.text: Mix the butter with the garlic, thyme leaves, zest of a lemon and salt.
Boil the whole cauliflower for 6 minutes, drain well and rub all over with the butter.
Roast at 200C on the oiled potatoes with the halved lemons, basting now and then, until deep golden.

Beat the cream cheese, butter, icing sugar and vanilla and spread over the warm scrolls.
